residualRisks: H1: loopback OAuth flow (start_oauth_server / poll_oauth_callback) has zero backend implementation — the entire strategy is dead code until the Rust commands are written and registered

H2: All cross-origin HTTP requests (server-picker probe, OAuth token exchange) use standard fetch instead of tauri-plugin-http's fetch — will fail on servers without CORS headers; @tauri-apps/plugin-http npm package is not even installed
M1+M2: ConfigStore silently drops writes on any I/O or serialization error, and non-atomic writes risk corruption on crash — user's server URL can be silently lost

childReport.manualNotes: Two HIGH-severity blockers found: (1) loopback OAuth backend commands are entirely missing from lib.rs, making that strategy dead code. (2) All cross-origin HTTP uses standard fetch instead of tauri-plugin-http's fetch, and the required npm package isn't installed. These are intent-vs-implementation mismatches where comments describe one approach but code implements another. The ConfigStore's silent write failure (M1) is the most impactful data-loss risk in production use.
